chemistry_notes.text: CuAAC [3+2] cycloaddition of benzyl azide with phenylacetylene over heterogeneous Cu/C CatCart. Rate-limiting step is metalacycle formation at the Cu surface. Flow advantage: packed-bed provides continuous intimate substrate-catalyst contact, eliminating diffusion limitation present in batch. Acetone bp = 56 degC; at 150 degC operating temperature, vapour pressure ~11.3 bar, so 20 bar BPR (only available setpoint) is mandatory and sufficient. The 4 mm ID CatCart is larger than ideal for plug-flow (Pe ~4, significant axial dispersion per calculations); this is accepted as the only available reactor. Residence time is set to 0.6 min (0.3 mL / 0.5 mL/min) as a starting screen point; a residence time screen from 0.1 to 1.0 mL/min (0.3-3 min) is recommended. Benzyl azide must be handled dilute (0.25 M) and behind blast shield at all times. Cu leaching from CatCart into product stream is a known risk and should be monitored by ICP-MS. No deoxygenation required. No light source required or available.

council_selection.text: Candidate 1 (combined score 0.807) edges candidate 2 (0.793) by 1.8%, within the 5% tiebreak band, so tiebreak criteria apply. Both candidates are identical in safety (1.000), geometry (1.000), and PVS (0.672); candidate 1 leads in chemistry (0.820 vs 0.760), kinetics (0.720 vs 0.680), and fluidics (0.820 vs 0.780), reflecting its slightly higher throughput and better alignment with the intensification screening objective. The researcher objective is a practical first flow experiment, not a demonstrated optimum; candidate 1 at Q=0.5 mL/min and τ=0.6 min is selected because its ±30% design envelope (Q: 0.35–0.65 mL/min, τ: 0.42–0.78 min) fully contains candidate 2's center point (Q=0.4 mL/min, τ=0.75 min), meaning a single run at candidate 1 conditions with a subsequent flow-rate screen naturally traverses both candidates' operating space. The most important remaining uncertainties are: (1) actual liquid holdup and true contact-time in the Cu/C CatCart packed bed — the 0.3 mL geometric volume is an upper bound on residence time, and bed voidage (unknown) will reduce effective τ; and (2) Cu leaching from the CatCart into the acetone product stream, which must be quantified by ICP-MS before any pharmaceutical application. The first bench experiment should verify that the system reaches steady state (confirmed by stable back-pressure and outlet concentration) within 3–5 reactor volumes (~1.5–2.5 min at 0.5 mL/min), then collect a sample for HPLC conversion analysis and ICP-MS Cu content; conversion and pressure drop are the primary go/no-go readouts. All conversion and productivity figures are unvalidated screening proxies derived from batch analogy kinetics and empty-tube hydraulic models that do not apply to this packed bed.

council_selection_justification.text: Candidate 1 (τ=0.6 min, Q=0.5 mL/min) is selected as the first screen experiment. It achieves a 5× residence-time reduction relative to the 3-min batch benchmark, approaching the 6× intensification hypothesis, while operating at the higher end of the pump's practical range (0.5 mL/min vs 0.4 mL/min for candidate 2). The researcher objective is a practical first flow experiment using only available equipment; candidate 1 provides a slightly more productive starting point (1867 mg/h proxy vs 1499 mg/h) and a wider ±30% operating envelope (Q: 0.35–0.65 mL/min) that accommodates lab variability without hitting the pump minimum floor. Both candidates are feasible screens; candidate 1 is preferred because its higher Q gives more headroom above the 0.1 mL/min pump minimum and its envelope fully spans the runner-up's center point, meaning a single screen at candidate 1 conditions implicitly brackets candidate 2 as well. The proposed flow advantage (hazardous-intermediate holdup reduction and productivity gain) is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated result; this is a SCREEN disposition.

source_record.text: Calculation estimated 0.3 min (range 0.2-0.5 min) based on 10x IF from batch 3 min. However, the 4 mm ID CatCart (inventory-mandated) has Pe ~4 (significant axial dispersion), so a longer residence time of 0.6 min is selected as the first screen point to compensate for non-ideal plug flow. This corresponds to 0.5 mL/min through 0.3 mL reactor. Analogy 1 (azide chemistry, PFA coil, 30 min at 120 degC) is not directly applicable due to different reactor type and lower temperature. Analogy 3 (thermal Claisen, 4 min at 195 degC) confirms that high-temperature flow can dramatically reduce batch times; our 0.6 min is consistent with this intensification direction. Screening 0.1-1.0 mL/min is recommended.
